first_finding.explanation: The two filter headers reported by the failed graph consume a filtered collection before the traversal has a value for it. In listResults, the candidate collection comes from readdirSync and each filename is tested for the .json suffix before path construction and sorting. In getLatestResult, the candidate collection is the path list returned by listResults, and the optional operation filter tests each path for the sanitized substring. Both filters need a defined entry value and a distinct collection of matches carried across iterations.
first_finding.suggestion: Use the acquired filenames and the returned path list as the respective traversal inputs. Initialize each match collection on entry and merge updates from the actual loop predecessors. Feed the completed first filter into path construction and sorting. Feed the completed second filter, or the original path list when no operation is supplied, into the empty-list check and first-path load.

validation_barriers.resolution: Correct this recorded review defect and revalidate it against the same selected source, operation and complete inventory.

locality.interpretation: Five independent Task findings were retained; one CFG finding was quarantined. This is local isolation, not whole-review evidence loss. Empty contract coverage reflects unavailable processing/annotation.

routing.explanation: Upstream and fragment repair both require accepted Task and graph. With no selected annotation and no accepted graph, every disjunct is false even though the review is partial with five usable Task findings. Fixing stage:graph target compatibility alone would not enter shared repair.
routing.policy_change_not_implied: Allowing repair without an accepted graph would be a separate explicit dependency/routing change requiring its own complete-source, ownership, budget and replay tests; it is not achieved by target aliasing.

previous_run_evidence.interpretation: The prior target gap existed unchanged before the last patch: generic failed-stage wording exceeded an annotation-only target allowlist. Graph failure newly exposed the gap. Five independent Task findings were retained; one graph finding was quarantined. Missing-CFG repair gating was a separate pre-existing blocker and cannot be solved by accepting a target name alone.
